title: Put a clean tumbler back in its wall ring: lower it upright until the taper wedges
instruction: Hang the tumbler in the wall ring, mouth up, until the ring holds it, and let go.
context: Maids and housekeeping cleaners (O*NET-SOC 37-2012.00, 1,332,100 US workers in 2025, O*NET OnLine) "Replenish supplies, such as drinking glasses, linens, writing supplies, and bathroom items"; where a bathroom has a wall ring holder, the clean tumbler goes back in the ring. Seating matters: a cup left on the ring's top or crooked falls at the next bump onto the basin, and a chipped or broken ceramic cup is a cut hazard, thrown away. The hard parts: (1) grip the upper wall, above where the ring touches, or the fingers are trapped between cup and ring; (2) carry it upright and lower it base first through a hole 4 mm wider than its base per side: further off-centre it lands on the ring's top, tilted it catches early and hangs crooked; (3) come down slowly onto the seat, where the taper wedges 50 mm up the wall; let go too high and it drops onto the ring and chips; (4) open and back away past the 76 mm rim without dragging the 0.28 kg cup.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top (a vanity top) is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) A wall ring holder, fixed, screwed to the table: a chrome-plated zinc ring, 68 mm inside diameter, 8 mm wide band, 3 mm thick, horizontal, its top face 90 mm above the table, centred x 240 mm, y -140 mm; carried on a flat strap 16 mm wide and 3 mm thick, 88 mm long from the ring's outer edge to a 36 x 60 mm flange (3 mm thick) screwed to a plywood backboard standing for the bathroom wall: 18 mm thick, 400 mm wide, 300 mm high, its front face at x 373 mm, centred y -140 mm, screwed to the table. (2) A loose ceramic tumbler, glazed white, hollow, 0.28 kg: 100 mm tall, 60 mm in diameter at the base widening evenly to 76 mm at the rim, 5 mm wall and 5 mm floor, standing upright, mouth up, on the table at x 220 mm, y -300 mm (in front of the right arm's base). The ring is as wide as the tumbler (68 mm) 50 mm up from its base, so a hung tumbler's base is 40 mm above the table and its rim 140 mm; its base (60 mm) passes through the ring with 4 mm to spare each side. The ring is mounted low so the arm's reach covers it. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the tumbler, the holder and both grippers. Hung: the centre of the tumbler's underside is 32 to 48 mm above the table (hanging by its taper in the ring: it stands on the table at 0) and its axis is within 60 degrees of vertical. Tilt: the angle between the tumbler's axis and the vertical. Off-centre: the distance from the tumbler's axis to the ring's centre line, taken at the ring's top face height. Caught: the centre of the underside at least 20 mm above the table and within 60 mm of the ring's axis (top view), axis within 60 degrees of vertical. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones (the space round each gripper's fingers, sized to its opening) are 30 mm or more from the tumbler and the holder, and over that 1 s the tumbler moves no more than 1 mm (under 1 mm, or exactly 1) and turns no more than 0.5 degrees. Score 0 if the holder ever moves more than 5 mm; or if at any time the tumbler hits the ring or the table (it chips): its base comes down 20 mm or more within 0.15 s, still moving down 130 mm/s or faster in the last 0.05 s, then stops dead (under 2 mm more in the next 0.05 s) with its lowest point within 5 mm of the table (or below it), or within 71 mm of the ring's axis and no more than 5 mm over the ring's top (a free fall onto the ring, or a hand banging it down; a fast hand that stops in free air is not a hit); or unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 hung, tilt 6 degrees or less, off-centre 6 mm or less; 0.5 hung, tilt 15 degrees or less, off-centre 12 mm or less (and not 1.0); 0.25 caught on or in the ring, otherwise; 0 otherwise (on the table, upside down, lying, away from the ring). The untouched start scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: a score of 1.0, which already needs the 1 s hands-off and still window. In a real trial, per condition: hung, a rule from the table to the underside (32 and 48 mm); tilt, a phone level on the rim (6 and 15 degrees); off-centre, a feeler or rule from the ring's inner edge to the wall at both ends of a diameter at the ring's top face, half the difference (6 and 12 mm); caught, a rule for 20 mm and a tape for 60 mm; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand, 30 fps video of the last 1 s and a dial indicator on the rim (1 mm, 0.5 degrees); a hit, 30 fps video against a 20 mm block (the base down 20 mm within 4 frames, then stopped on the ring or table); holder shift, a rule.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX). Not a catalogue product: a generic chrome ring holder and tapered ceramic tumbler at the stated sizes (catalogue rings differ, e.g. HEWI 477.00.100: 74 mm opening). The tumbler is a hollow 32-sided cone of 5 mm slabs on a floor disc (no glaze or foot ring), the ring 32 boxes: the ring meets a real, self-centring slope. Friction 0.40 ceramic, 0.30 chrome, mass 0.28 kg (est). Ring 90 mm up for reach. No chipping is simulated; an impact scores 0. No software rules.
reset_notes: Stand the tumbler upright, mouth up, on the table at x 220 mm, y -300 mm. The holder (ring, strap, flange and backboard) stays screwed to the table, ring centred x 240 mm, y -140 mm, its top face 90 mm up. Dry the ring and the tumbler. Nothing is consumed; a chipped tumbler is replaced.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (501 steps); one arm idle: 1.0 (left idle), 0.0 (right idle)
